# Work with tensions from the command line

In this tutorial you will learn the tension lifecycle with the `glassfrog tension`
commands: capture a tension you have sensed, find it again, read its detail, edit
it, and finally retire it. A tension is the seed of a governance proposal, so this
is the first half of the governance write path.

By the end you will be able to record what you notice in your circle and manage it
from capture through to retirement, all without leaving the terminal.

## Prerequisites

- The `glassfrog` CLI installed and on your `PATH`.
- A configured API token. If you have not set one up, do the authentication
  tutorial first (`docs/guides/authentication/tutorial.md`).
- A role id to sense against. You can find one with `glassfrog me roles` (the
  roles you fill) or `glassfrog roles` (the whole organization).

This tutorial assumes your token is already in place.

## Step 1 — Capture a tension

Record a tension against the role that senses it. The body is required — it is the
substance of what you noticed:

```
glassfrog tension create role_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef \
  --body "Scheduling decisions keep stalling without a clear owner"
```

The role you name is the *sensing role*; the *sensing person* is recorded
automatically from your token — you never type your own name. On success the
command produces the created tension, including its `ten_` id and its status (the
server computes that for you).

You can add a short title and a routing hint at capture:

```
glassfrog tension create role_0123…  \
  --body "Scheduling decisions keep stalling" \
  --label "Scheduling ownership" \
  --meeting-type governance
```

Capture the `ten_` id with `-o json` and read `data.id` — you will need it for the
later steps.

## Step 2 — Find your tension again

List the tensions a role is carrying:

```
glassfrog tension list role_0123…
```

In a busy circle, narrow to just the unworked ones:

```
glassfrog tension list role_0123…  --status unprocessed
```

If you are facilitating a circle and want to see what every circle *inside* it is
sensing — not the circle's own tensions, but its direct sub-roles' — roll them up
in one read:

```
glassfrog tension subroles role_0123…
```

## Step 3 — Read one tension in full

Once you have a `ten_` id, read its complete detail:

```
glassfrog tension get ten_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
```

This shows the body, label, status, meeting-type, and the sensing role and person
— everything recorded about that one tension.

## Step 4 — Edit a tension

Tensions are editable after capture. Fix the wording, retitle it, or reroute it —
supply only the fields you want to change:

```
glassfrog tension update ten_0123…  --body "Scheduling decisions stall without a Scheduler role"
glassfrog tension update ten_0123…  --meeting-type tactical
```

Unlike capture, update can also move a tension through its lifecycle. When you have
finished working a tension, mark it done by moving it to `archived`:

```
glassfrog tension update ten_0123…  --status archived
```

An update must change at least one field — running `tension update` with no field
flags is rejected before any request.

## Step 5 — Discard a tension you no longer need

If a tension was captured by mistake or no longer belongs on the active record,
remove it:

```
glassfrog tension discard ten_0123…
```

This is a soft-delete — the record is marked, not erased, and any proposals
attached to the tension are left in place. The command is deliberately retry-safe:
running it again on an already-gone tension still exits successfully, and it tells
you on stderr whether it discarded a live tension or found it already gone.

## What you've learned

You have run the full tension lifecycle: captured a tension against a sensing role,
listed and rolled up tensions to find it, read its detail, edited and archived it,
and discarded one you no longer needed. You saw that the server owns the status and
the sensing person, and that the CLI simply records what you sense and surfaces
what the API returns.

From here:

- A captured tension is the anchor for a proposal — continue into the
  [proposal tutorial](../proposals/tutorial.md) to turn it into a governance
  change.
- For every flag, filter, and exit code, see the
  [Tensions reference](../../reference/tensions.md).
- To understand *why* discard treats a missing tension as success and why the CLI
  never sets status on capture, see
  [Understanding tensions](../../explanation/understanding-tensions.md).
